claims.claim_ar: جواب السائل محذوف - أي أن جواب سؤال (أَرَأَيْتُمْ ...) محذوف في السِّياق القصصي
claims.claim_en: The expected reply is omitted — the answer to the implied question (e.g. 'أَرَأَيْتُمْ ...') is left out in the narrative (ellipsis of reply).
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates immediacy and leaves the consequence to the hearer's inference; compresses the narrative to focus on the objection and response.

claims.claim_ar: حذف العاطف في السرد (حذف حرف العطف الوارد عادة) عند توالي الأقوال لتحريك السرد وتسريع النقل
claims.claim_en: Omission of the coordinating element (the 'ʿāṭif') — the conjunction that might normally link clauses is omitted in the narrative, producing a brisk, compressed sequence.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Condenses the account and tightens the sequence of reported speech, giving a sense of direct, uninterrupted utterance.

claims.source_quote_ar: صيغة العود تستدعى رجوع العائد إلى حال كان عليها قبل
claims.claim_ar: استعمال صيغة العود (لَتَعُودُنَّ) هنا مذكور أنه قد يُفهم على أنها تستدعي الرجوع، لكن الزمخشري يبيّن أنّها كثيرًا ما تُستخدم بمعنى "صار" (التبدّل) لا بالضرورة رجوع إلى حالة سابقة — استعمال شبه مجازي أو انتقالي للصيغة.
claims.claim_en: The use of the verb form of 'return' (لَتَعُودُنَّ) is discussed as conventionally suggesting 'return', but al-Zamakhshari notes it is often used in the sense of 'become' (صار) rather than literal return — a figurative/transfer usage of the form.
claims.needs_review_reason: Interpretive classification as 'majaz' (figurative use) relies on al-Zamakhshari's semantic discussion; another commentator might prefer a different ma'na-label.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Permits a stronger threat/possibility reading (becoming like them) without committing to a literal temporal return; increases semantic force and ambiguity.

claims.claim_ar: وجود تعريف للخبر وإقحام فصل/وقفة في البنية (إدخال فصل لتعريف الخبر وتأكيد الضمير المتصل)، أي توظيف الفصل والتعريف لخفض أو زيادة الإيقاع البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: Insertion of a pause/partition and definition of the predicate is used to emphasize and confirm the attached pronoun — a deliberate use of pause (fasl) vs. linkage (wasl) in the phrasing.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Emphatic segmentation that highlights the predicate and the pronoun, reinforcing the threat and the social stance of the speakers.

claims.source_quote_ar: تخييرهم إياه أدب حسن راعوه معه
claims.claim_ar: استخدام حرف العطف/الاختيار 'أَوْ' هنا بوظيفة تخيير — عرض خيار/مراعاة أدبية تجاه المخاطب.
claims.claim_en: Use of the disjunctive 'أَوْ' functions as offering a choice — a politeness/mitigating rhetorical move in the address.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Softens the threat by framing alternatives as an offered choice, reflecting social tact or rhetorical moderation.

claims.source_quote_ar: لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتصيرن كفاراً مثلنا
claims.claim_ar: مقابلة بين احتمالَي الإخراج أو التحول إلى الكفر — توازي/مقابلة بلاغية (عرض خيارين متقابلين في صيغة مكّنة ومؤكدة).
claims.claim_en: A rhetorical pairing (muqabalah) contrasts two presented alternatives — being expelled or becoming like them in disbelief — creating a parallel/antithetical structure.
claims.needs_review_reason: Al-Zamakhshari's paraphrase is used as source; classification as 'muqabalah' (badi) is interpretive on the parallelism between the two alternatives.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Sets two dire outcomes in parallel to magnify the pressure and to present the speakers' ultimatum as a stark binary choice.

warnings: All source quotes and notes provided are from al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) chunks only; the requested set of commentators (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha sections) were not supplied. Additional sources may yield further or different rhetorical readings.

Some classifications (e.g. labeling the use of لَتَعُودُنَّ as 'majaz' or the pairing as 'muqabalah') are interpretive and drawn from al-Zamakhshari's discussion; these may require review against other commentators or a stricter taxonomy.

I avoided morphological/grammatical observations and focused on rhetorical devices per instructions; if you prefer different device-mappings (e.g. classifying certain phenomena under other branch/subtypes), indicate the preferred taxonomy.
